column1: synonym|/ˈsɪnənɪm/|语义学|n. 同义词|The thesaurus lists a synonym after each difficult headword.|thesaurus 在每个难词后列出一个同义词。
antonym|/ˈæntənɪm/|语义学|n. 反义词|Students learned an antonym to expand their active vocabulary.|学生学习反义词以扩充积极词汇量。
lexicon|/ˈleksɪkən/|语义学|n. 词汇库，语汇|His personal lexicon grew richer through wide and patient reading.|他通过广泛而耐心的阅读使个人词汇库更丰富。
syntax|/ˈsɪntæks/|语义学|n. 句法|Clear syntax helps readers follow a complex argument with ease.|清晰的句法帮助读者轻松跟上复杂的论证。
phoneme|/ˈfəʊniːm/|语义学|n. 音位|The linguist analysed each phoneme in the recorded political speech.|语言学家分析了录音政治演讲中的每个音位。
morpheme|/ˈmɔːfiːm/|语义学|n. 词素|The word unhappiness contains three separate morpheme units.|unhappiness 一词包含三个独立的词素单位。
discourse|/ˈdɪskɔːs/|语义学|n. 语篇，论述|Academic discourse demands clarity and well supported firm claims.|学术语篇要求清晰且有充分支撑的论点。
rhetoric|/ˈretərɪk/|语义学|n. 修辞，修辞学|Political rhetoric often appeals to emotion over reason.|政治修辞常常诉诸情感而非理性。
ambiguity|/æmˈbɪɡjuəti/|语义学|n. 歧义|The ambiguity of the clause confused the careful young readers.|该从句的歧义让细心的年轻读者感到困惑。
polysemy|/pəˈlɪsɪmi/|语义学|n. 一词多义|Polysemy explains why one word carries several related senses.|一词多义解释了一个词为何具有多个相关义项。
utterance|/ˈʌtərəns/|语义学|n. 话语，言说|Her sudden utterance broke the long silence in the class.|她突然的话语打破了课堂上长久的沉默。
signifier|/ˈsɪɡnɪfaɪə/|语义学|n. 能指|The word tree is the signifier for the concept of a tree.|tree 这个词是树这一概念的能指。
referent|/ˈrefərənt/|语义学|n. 指称对象|The referent of he was the boy who entered the room.|he 的指称对象是走进房间的那个男孩。
dialect|/ˈdaɪəlekt/|语义学|n. 方言|The novel captures the local dialect with striking total authenticity.|这部小说以惊人地道的笔触再现了当地方言。
etymology|/ˌetɪˈmɒlədʒi/|语义学|n. 词源|The etymology of the term reveals its ancient Greek origin.|该词的词源揭示了它古老的希腊语根源。
homonym|/ˈhɒmənɪm/|语义学|n. 同形异义词|The homonym bank means both a river side and a bank.|同形异义词 bank 既指河岸也指银行。
hyperbole|/haɪˈpɜːbəli/|语义学|n. 夸张法|His claim was obvious hyperbole rather than literal truth.|他的说法明显是夸张而非字面的事实。
irony|/ˈaɪrəni/|语义学|n. 反讽|The irony lay in his praising the very thing he hated.|反讽在于他称赞了自己最厌恶的东西。
satire|/ˈsætaɪə/|语义学|n. 讽刺作品|The film uses satire to expose the folly of vain pride.|影片用讽刺揭露虚荣的愚蠢。
pun|/pʌn/|语义学|n. 双关语|A clever pun can make a dull lecture far more memorable.|巧妙的双关语能让枯燥的讲座更令人难忘。
innuendo|/ˌɪnjuˈendəʊ/|语义学|n. 暗讽，影射|The speech was full of innuendo about his known rivals.|演讲充满了对知名对手的影射。
semantics|/sɪˈmæntɪks/|语义学|n. 语义学|Semantics studies how meaning is constructed in language.|语义学研究意义如何在语言中构建。
pragmatics|/præɡˈmætɪks/|语义学|n. 语用学|Pragmatics examines meaning in actual social context.|语用学考察真实社会语境中的意义。
wording|/ˈwɜːdɪŋ/|语义学|n. 措辞|The careful wording avoided any hint of direct blame.|谨慎的措辞避免了任何直接指责的意味。
paraphrase|/ˈpærəfreɪz/|语义学|v. 释义，改述|Please paraphrase the passage in your own simple words.|请用你自己的话简明地释义这段文章。
acronym|/ˈækrənɪm/|语义学|n. 首字母缩略词|NATO is a common acronym for a military alliance.|NATO 是一个军事联盟的常用首字母缩略词。
abbreviation|/əˌbriːviˈeɪʃn/|语义学|n. 缩写|The abbreviation etc appears frequently in informal class notes.|缩写 etc 在非正式课堂笔记中频繁出现。
idiom|/ˈɪdiəm/|语义学|n. 习语|The idiom kick the bucket means to die in plain slang.|习语 kick the bucket 在俚语中意为死亡。
proverb|/ˈprɒvɜːb/|语义学|n. 谚语|The proverb warns that haste makes waste in all work.|这句谚语告诫人们欲速则不达。
slang|/slæŋ/|语义学|n. 俚语|Teenage slang changes faster than formal written usage.|青少年俚语比正式书面语变化更快。
register|/ˈredʒɪstə/|语义学|n. 语域|The formal register suits an academic essay best.|正式语域最适合学术论文。
intonation|/ˌɪntəˈneɪʃn/|语义学|n. 语调|Her rising intonation turned the statement into a question.|她上扬的语调把陈述变成了疑问。
syllable|/ˈsɪləbl/|语义学|n. 音节|The word camera has three distinct syllable in speech.|camera 一词在口语中有三个清晰的音节。
consonant|/ˈkɒnsənənt/|语义学|n. 辅音|The final consonant softens in some regional accents.|词尾辅音在某些地方口音中弱化。
vowel|/ˈvaʊəl/|语义学|n. 元音|The long vowel changes the meaning of the whole word.|长元音改变了整个词的含义。
tense|/tens/|语义学|n. 时态|The past tense shows the action happened before now.|过去时态表示动作发生在现在之前。
pronoun|/ˈprəʊnaʊn/|语义学|n. 代词|The pronoun she replaced the noun without losing sense.|代词 she 替代名词而不失原意。
preposition|/ˌprepəˈzɪʃn/|语义学|n. 介词|The preposition in links the verb to its object place.|介词 in 把动词与其宾语位置连接起来。
conjunction|/kənˈdʒʌŋkʃn/|语义学|n. 连词|The conjunction but signals a contrast between two ideas.|连词 but 表示两种观点之间的对比。
adjective|/ˈædʒɪktɪv/|语义学|n. 形容词|The adjective red modifies the noun apple directly.|形容词 red 直接修饰名词 apple。
adverb|/ˈædvɜːb/|语义学|n. 副词|The adverb quickly tells us more about the verb ran.|副词 quickly 进一步说明动词 ran。
verb|/vɜːb/|语义学|n. 动词|A verb expresses the main action in a clear sentence.|动词在清晰的句子中表达主要动作。
noun|/naʊn/|语义学|n. 名词|A noun often names a person place or concrete thing.|名词常指人、地点或具体事物。
lexeme|/ˈleksiːm/|语义学|n. 词位|Each lexeme represents one abstract unit of meaning.|每个词位代表一个抽象的意义单位。
presupposition|/ˌpriːsʌpəˈzɪʃn/|语义学|n. 预设|The presupposition of the question was never stated openly.|这个问题的预设从未被公开说明。
implication|/ˌɪmplɪˈkeɪʃn/|语义学|n. 蕴含，言外之意|The implication of his remark worried the whole committee.|他话语的言外之意让整个委员会担忧。
allegory|/ˈæləɡəri/|语义学|n. 寓言|The allegory compares life to a long hard sea voyage.|这则寓言把人生比作漫长艰难的航程。
metonymy|/mɪˈtɒnəmi/|语义学|n. 转喻|Metonymy uses crown to stand for royal power.|转喻用 crown 指代王权。
colloquialism|/kəˈləʊkwiəlɪzəm/|语义学|n. 口语表达|The essay avoided colloquialism to keep a serious tone.|文章避免使用口语表达以保持严肃语气。
neologism|/niˈɒlədʒɪzəm/|语义学|n. 新词|The neologism soon entered everyday online conversation.|这个新词很快进入日常网络交流。
jargon|/ˈdʒɑːɡən/|语义学|n. 行话|Medical jargon often baffles patients without medical training.|医学行话常让未经医学训练的患者困惑。
cliche|/ˈkliːʃeɪ/|语义学|n. 陈词滥调|The cliche added nothing new to the tired old debate.|这句陈词滥调给老套的辩论毫无新意。
oxymoron|/ˌɒksɪˈmɔːrɒn/|语义学|n. 矛盾修饰法|The oxymoron deafening silence is striking and memorable.|矛盾修饰法 deafening silence 醒目且令人难忘。
euphemism|/ˈjuːfəmɪzəm/|语义学|n. 委婉语|The euphemism passed away softens the hard fact of death.|委婉语 passed away 弱化了死亡这一硬事实。
simile|/ˈsɪməli/|语义学|n. 明喻|The simile compares hope to a small bright flame.|这个明喻把希望比作一小簇明亮的火焰。
contradiction|/ˌkɒntrəˈdɪkʃn/|论证谬误|n. 矛盾|His statement contained a clear contradiction with his earlier claim.|他的陈述与先前的说法存在明显矛盾。
paradox|/ˈpærədɒks/|论证谬误|n. 悖论|The paradox puzzled readers who expected a simple answer.|这个悖论让期待简单答案的读者困惑。
strawman|/ˈstrɔːmæn/|论证谬误|n. 稻草人谬误|He used a strawman by misstating his opponent real view.|他用稻草人谬误歪曲了对手的真实观点。
equivocate|/ɪˈkwɪvəkeɪt/|论证谬误|v. 含糊其辞|The witness tried to equivocate to avoid a direct answer.|证人试图含糊其辞以回避直接回答。
syllogism|/ˈsɪlədʒɪzəm/|论证谬误|n. 三段论|A valid syllogism leads from two premises to a conclusion.|有效的三段论从两个前提推出结论。
rebut|/rɪˈbʌt/|论证谬误|v. 反驳|She used strong evidence to rebut the careless accusation.|她用有力证据反驳了草率的指控。
verify|/ˈverɪfaɪ/|论证谬误|v. 核实|You must verify each claim before accepting it as fact.|你必须核实每个论点才能把它当作事实。
falsify|/ˈfɔːlsɪfaɪ/|论证谬误|v. 篡改，证伪|To falsify data is a serious breach of academic honesty.|篡改数据是严重违反学术诚信的行为。
overgeneralise|/ˌəʊvəˈdʒenrəlaɪz/|论证谬误|v. 过度概括|Do not overgeneralise from one unusual case to all people.|不要从一个异常个案过度概括到所有人。
circular|/ˈsɜːkjələ/|论证谬误|adj. 循环论证的|His proof was circular and therefore failed to convince us.|他的证明是循环论证，因此未能说服我们。
presuppose|/ˌpriːsəˈpəʊz/|论证谬误|v. 预设|The plan presuppose that everyone will cooperate willingly.|该计划预设人人都会自愿配合。
invalidate|/ɪnˈvælɪdeɪt/|论证谬误|v. 使无效|New evidence may invalidate the conclusion we drew too fast.|新证据可能使我们草率得出的结论失效。
adhominem|/ˌædˈhɒmɪnem/|论证谬误|adj. 人身攻击的|An adhominem reply attacks the person not the argument.|人身攻击式回应攻击的是人而非论点。
nonsequitur|/ˌnɒnˈsekwtə/|论证谬误|n. 不相关推论|His sudden change of topic was a blatant nonsequitur.|他突然转换话题是一个明显的不相关推论。
postulate|/ˈpɒstjəleɪt/|论证谬误|v. 假定|We can postulate a cause but must still test it carefully.|我们可以假定一个原因，但仍须仔细检验。
rationalise|/ˈræʃnəlaɪz/|论证谬误|v. 文过饰非|He tried to rationalise a choice that was plainly unfair.|他试图为明显不公的选择文过饰非。
specious|/ˈspiːʃəs/|论证谬误|adj. 似是而非的|A specious argument may fool those who do not look closer.|似是而非的论点可能骗过不细看的人。
spurious|/ˈspjʊəriəs/|论证谬误|adj. 站不住脚的|The spurious claim collapsed under simple factual scrutiny.|这个站不住脚的论断在简单核实下崩塌。
hasty|/ˈheɪsti/|论证谬误|adj. 草率的|His hasty judgement ignored evidence that did not fit.|他草率的判断忽略了不符的证据。
anecdotal|/ˌænɪkˈdəʊtl/|论证谬误|adj. 轶事性的|Anecdotal stories are weak proof of a general trend.|轶事性故事不足以证明普遍趋势。
cognitive|/ˈkɒɡnətɪv/|论证谬误|adj. 认知的|Cognitive bias can distort how we read the same fact.|认知偏差会扭曲我们解读同一事实的方式。
heuristic|/hjʊˈrɪstɪk/|论证谬误|adj. 启发式的|A heuristic rule helps thinking but admits clear exceptions.|启发式规则有助于思考但有明显例外。
dialectic|/ˌdaɪəˈlektɪk/|论证谬误|n. 辩证（法）|The dialectic moved from thesis through antithesis to synthesis.|辩证法从正题经反题走向合题。
thesis|/ˈθiːsɪs/|论证谬误|n. 论点，命题|Her central thesis was that habits shape our character.|她的核心论点是习惯塑造品格。
antithesis|/ænˈtɪθɪsɪs/|论证谬误|n. 反题|The antithesis challenged the comfortable assumption we held.|反题挑战了我们安逸的预设。
assertion|/əˈsɜːʃn/|论证谬误|n. 断言|Every bold assertion needs support from solid evidence.|每个大胆断言都需要坚实证据支撑。
proposition|/ˌprɒpəˈzɪʃn/|论证谬误|n. 主张|The proposition was debated by both sides at length.|该主张被双方充分辩论。
argument|/ˈɑːɡjumənt/|论证谬误|n. 论证|The argument rested on a premise that few would accept.|该论证基于一个很少有人接受的前提。
claim|/kleɪm/|论证谬误|n. 主张|The claim must be tested before we treat it as true.|该主张须经验证才能被视为真。
sound|/saʊnd/|论证谬误|adj. 合理的（论证）|A sound argument is both valid and has true premises.|合理的论证既有效又前提为真。
cogent|/ˈkəʊdʒənt/|论证谬误|adj. 有说服力的|Her cogent reasoning won over the skeptical committee members.|她有说服力的推理赢得了怀疑者的支持。
plausible|/ˈplɔːzəbl/|论证谬误|adj. 貌似合理的|A plausible excuse may still hide the real motive.|貌似合理的借口仍可能掩盖真正动机。
tenable|/ˈtenəbl/|论证谬误|adj. 站得住脚的|The position is no longer tenable after the new findings.|新发现后该立场不再站得住脚。
defensible|/dɪˈfensəbl/|论证谬误|adj. 可辩护的|Only a defensible view survives serious open criticism.|只有可辩护的观点才能经得起严肃公开批评。
discount|/dɪsˈkaʊnt/|论证谬误|v. 低估，忽视|We should not discount evidence that weakens our favourite theory.|我们不应忽视削弱偏爱理论的证据。
misrepresent|/ˌmɪsreprɪˈzent/|论证谬误|v. 歪曲|He tried to misrepresent the study to fit his agenda.|他试图歪曲研究以迎合自己的议程。
oversimplify|/ˌəʊvəˈsɪmplɪfaɪ/|论证谬误|v. 过度简化|Do not oversimplify a complex issue into two neat sides.|不要把复杂问题过度简化为两方。
conflate|/kənˈfleɪt/|论证谬误|v. 混淆|Careless writers conflate correlation with real causation.|粗心的写作者把相关与因果混为一谈。
sophistry|/ˈsɒfɪstri/|论证谬误|n. 诡辩|Sophistry dresses weak points in clever sounding language.|诡辩用巧妙的语言包装薄弱之处。
reasoning|/ˈriːznɪŋ/|论证谬误|n. 推理|Faulty reasoning produced a conclusion nobody could accept.|错误的推理得出无人能接受的结论。
posthoc|/ˌpəʊstˈhɒk/|论证谬误|adj. 事后归因的|The posthoc error assumes the earlier event caused the later.|事后归因错误假定先发生者导致后发生者。
slippery|/ˈslɪpəri/|论证谬误|adj. 滑坡的|The slippery slope claim warned of a chain of disasters.|滑坡论声称一连串灾难将会发生。
irrational|/ɪˈræʃnəl/|论证谬误|adj. 非理性的|An irrational fear of change blocked the useful reform.|对非理性的变革恐惧阻碍了有益改革。
dogma|/ˈdɒɡmə/|论证谬误|n. 教条|Blind dogma resists any evidence that questions its truth.|盲目教条抗拒任何质疑其真实性的证据。
apriori|/ˌeɪpraɪˈɔːraɪ/|论证谬误|adj. 先验的|An apriori claim needs confirmation from observed facts.|先验主张需要观察事实来确认。
sceptic|/ˈskeptɪk/|论证谬误|n. 怀疑论者|The sceptic demanded proof before believing the strange tale.|怀疑论者要求证据才信这奇异说法。
falsifiable|/ˈfɔːlsɪfaɪəbl/|论证谬误|adj. 可证伪的|A good theory must be falsifiable by some possible test.|好理论必须能被某种可能的检验证伪。
conjecture|/kənˈdʒektʃə/|论证谬误|n. 推测|Her conjecture was interesting but lacked firm supporting data.|她的推测有趣但缺乏坚实数据支撑。
analogy|/əˈnælədʒi/|论证谬误|n. 类比|The analogy clarified the point but was no strict proof.|这个类比阐明了观点但并非严格证明。
inductive|/ɪnˈdʌktɪv/|论证谬误|adj. 归纳的|Inductive reasoning draws general rules from observed cases.|归纳推理从观察个案得出一般规则。
deductive|/dɪˈdʌktɪv/|论证谬误|adj. 演绎的|Deductive logic moves from general law to a clear case.|演绎逻辑从一般法则推至一个个案。
contention|/kənˈtenʃn/|论证谬误|n. 争论点|The main contention was whether the law was truly fair.|主要争论点在于该法律是否真正公平。
refutation|/ˌrefjuˈteɪʃn/|论证谬误|n. 反驳|The refutation exposed a hidden flaw in the bold claim.|反驳暴露了该大胆主张中的隐蔽缺陷。
warrant|/ˈwɒrənt/|论证谬误|n. 理据|The warrant links the evidence to the claim it supports.|理据把证据与它所支撑的主张联系起来。
backing|/ˈbækɪŋ/|论证谬误|n. 支撑|The backing strengthened the warrant with further solid fact.|支撑用更多事实加强了理据。
methodology|/ˌmeθəˈdɒlədʒi/|学术名词|n. 方法论|The methodology section explained how the data was gathered.|方法论部分说明了数据如何收集。
epistemology|/ɪˌpɪstɪˈmɒlədʒi/|学术名词|n. 认识论|Epistemology asks how we can know what is truly real.|认识论追问我们如何知道何为真。
ontology|/ɒnˈtɒlədʒi/|学术名词|n. 本体论|Ontology studies what kinds of things fundamentally exist.|本体论研究哪些事物根本上存在。
statistic|/stəˈtɪstɪk/|学术名词|n. 统计量|A single statistic can mislead if taken out of context.|单个统计量脱离语境会误导人。
